ENDBOX
P	The town of Marshedge lies along the <b>Highway</b> (page 270), on a rise overlooking <b>Ferrier's Fen</b> (page 116). Many consider Marshedgers insane to live so close to such a dangerous place, but long ago, some of them learned the ways of the Fen and of bendis root, the burning of which keeps unclean things at bay.
H2	Questions
Q	Which of the Old Families (Ferrier, Hawtrey, Tricklebank, Eldershaw) have you dealt with most? How so?
Q	What trouble did Brennan's Claws cause you, back in their bandit days?
Q	Do they worship ____ here? How?
Q	Who do you look forward to seeing?
Q	Who are you hoping to avoid?
Q	What's the oddest rumor you've heard about the fen-walkers?
Q	As you enter, what's the most striking difference between here and Stonetop?
H2	Places
HR
B	<b>The Hill</b>, around which the town huddles, looming over Ferrier's Fen. Riddled with <b>Maker</b>-ruins (page 264).
B	<b>The Palisade</b> surrounds the town, with braziers of bendis root burning day and night. Four members of <b>the Guard</b> (page 276) walk the ramparts.
B	<b>The Sruth</b>, a wide, shallow river that drains lazily past Marshedge and into the Fen. Lined with reeds and willows, the bed made of loose, sucking mud.
B	<b>The Bridge</b>, a wooden span across the Sruth where a stretch of road once lay, just wide enough for a wagon. A pair of Guards collect tolls at the gate house.
B	<b>Low Town</b>, hovels of the working folk, all around the Hill and Edgemarket. Wattle and daub construction, cramped gardens, dirty kids, lots of livestock. Guards don't patrol here.
B	<b>Edgemarket</b>, on a <b>wayside</b> (page 271) near the middle of town, crowded with tents, wagons, merchants, and visitors. Surrounded by shops, a pair of pubs, and a few traveler-houses. Patrolled by a pair of Guards.
PAGE	275
B	<b>The Mire</b>, a muddy slum north of the main palisade, poking into the Fen. Wood walkways stretch between bogs of rice and herbs. Two gates link it to Low Town, each manned by a Guard.
B	<b>Dropoff</b>, middle-class homes and shops all around the slope of the Hill. A pair of Guards are always on patrol.
B	<b>High Town</b>, a neighborhood of stone buildings with slate roofs atop the Hill. Where the <b>Old Families</b> (page 276) live. Ringed by a second palisade, with a pair of Guards always watching the gate.
B	<b>The Garrison</b>, the Guard's headquarters, just outside High Town. A dozen or so Guards are stationed here at any time, off-duty but on-call.
B	<b>Eastgate</b>, where the Highway passes through the palisade and farmers come and go to the fields. A pair of Guards collect tolls from visitors.
B	<b>Miller's Hill</b>, a Maker-ruin just east of town, repurposed into a windmill. Everyone mumbles about how the place is haunted. It is.
B	<b>The Fields</b>, stretching away to the east and south, owned by the Old Families. Some outbuildings, plenty of livestock, but few inhabitants.
H2	Ruins of the past
HR
P	This was clearly a place of importance in the time of the Makers. Their ruins dot the Hill and extend deep below. Some of these tunnels are used as storehouses or mausoleums. Others are unexplored.
P	What was this place, originally? That's for you to decide, but perhaps it was…
E	a <b>Stone Lord</b> (page 382) outpost, standing watch over Ferrier's Fen;
E	the edge of a <b>Green Lord</b> (page 210) city, all that's left after the Stone Lords sank much of their lands;
E	a center of trade between Green Lords and Stone Lords, abandoned when war broke out between them;
E	a Stone Lord manor, reclaimed by the <b>Barrow Builders</b> (page 34);
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
P	Whatever you decide, consider writing it up as a site, with dangers and discoveries that might now be in the hands of the Old Families, the Guilds, and/or Brennan.

H2	Names
HR
P	Irish-inspired: Abben, Ailen, Brin, Brogan, Catlin, Coln, Daedre, Dermos, Ennin, Finnen, Gilor, Isbeal, Kiran, Lile, Lim, Mathuin, Mirne, Noren, Owan, Ragan, Renan, Seadha, Seann, Tierney, Ulliam
P	Marshedge and Stonetop share a language but the dialects are quite distinct, implying some common but distant ancestry.
H2	People
HR
ICON	icons/person.svg
P	<b>Brennan</b>, onetime bandit leader of the Claws, now the town's marshal.
P	The Council thought it'd be cheaper and easier to pay him to guard the town than to hunt him down and defeat him.
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Guard</b>, the town's well-drilled standing watch. Tensions exist between the ex-Claws, old-timer loyalists, and the new recruits. (~40 guards total)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Old Families</b> dwell in the stone manor houses of High Town and have a piece of every pie. (~30 family members and another ~40 servants)
B2	The Ferriers have lost much clout in recent years. Their matriarch, Ianthe, is ailing but still sharp (<b>Instinct</b> to maintain her family's dignity).
B2	The Hawtrey patriarch, Muiris, is one of Brennan's main allies (<b>Instinct</b> to put his family's fortunes above all else).
B2	The Tricklebanks resent the Ferrier's prestige. Led by cagey old Caineach (<b>Instinct</b> to sieze any opportunity).
B2	The Eldershaws have a reputation for being tough yet honorable, but an untimely death has left young Ailbe in charge (<b>Instinct</b> to put off decisions).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Guilds</b>, comprised of weavers, potters, glassblowers, and herbalists. They generate much of the town's wealth, and chafe at the Old Families' power. (~125 artisans, assistants, and families)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The lesser trades</b>—smiths, bakers, carpenters, thatchers, the miller, and others who keep the town running. (~40 artisans, assistants, and families)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Fen-walkers</b> (page 117) ply the wetlands, gathering herbs, hunting game, cutting peat and clay, and keeping tabs on the <b>suarachan</b> (page 124). They recruit from orphans and those with no prospects. Some have (and hide) weird mutations. (~20 souls)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Council</b>, Marshedge's governing body. Includes the head of each Old Family, the master of each Guild, the eldest of the fen-walkers, and Brennan (who has no vote, but pushes them around).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Merchants</b> are key to the town's prosperity. Mostly local, but a few have settled here from afar. (~40 souls)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Beggars & thieves</b> gather in Edgemarket, along the Highway, and in Dropoff, seeking sympathy or easy marks. (~20-40 souls, varies by day)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Farmers & laborers</b> make up the rest of town. Mostly tenant farmers, put-upon homemakers, and muscle for hire hoping to earn rent. (~500 souls)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Travelers</b> come to trade at Edgemarket, to consult with herbalists, or to seek (or spend) their fortunes. They stay with local contacts, in their own wagons, or at one of a few traveler-houses. (~25-100 souls, depending on the season)
PAGE	277
H2	Secrets
HR
B	The town charter gives fen-walkers the right to demand aid from any resident, and the responsibility to execute those found to be "corrupted by vile spirits, or congressing with such."
B	Every seven years, one of the Old Families delivers one of their children to the <b>Willow Witches</b> (page 120). A fen-walker leaves the child at one of the grand willow trees, never looking back. Rarely, such a child returns, years later, and greatly changed.
B	The miller's wife is a <b>necromancer</b> (page 84), with a number of ghosts bound in the basement. Brennan knows her secret and has taken to consulting her.
B	You don't just start begging or thieving in Marshedge; there's a guild to join, rules to follow, and fees to pay. Surely Brennan and the Guard are compensated for looking the other way.
H2	Hooks
B	A daughter of the Old Families tries to save her son from the Willow Witches.
B	A fen-walker discovers a ruin, home to a fell beast but also great treasure.
B	Idealists attempt to organize and get recognition for a Farmers Guild.
B	A High Town merchant has what the PCs seek; but seeks exclusive rights to trading Stonetop whisky in exchange.
B	A spurned Guild apprentice is sending dark spirits against their old master
B	A well-regarded loyalist of the old Guard has gone missing. His granddaughter asks the PCs for help.

H2	Moves
HR
P	<b>ASK AROUND</b>
P	When you <b><i>spend a purse of coppers and a</i></b> <b><i>few hours asking around town</i></b>, say what you hope to learn and roll +CHA: <b>on a 10+</b>, you get a clear and useful answer; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you get an answer but pick 1:
B	It's incomplete, contradictory, or unclear, ask the GM how you could learn more
B	It'll cost you another purse of coppers
B	You've drawn unwanted attention or gotten yourself embroiled in a situation of the GM's choosing
HR
P	<b>CAROUSE</b>
P	When you <b><i>spend a handful of silvers having</i></b> <b><i>a good time</i></b>, roll +CHA: <b>on a 10+</b>, pick 2;
P	<b>on a 7-9</b>, pick 1:
B	You spread a rumor or tale far and wide
B	You make a loyal new friend
B	You learn something useful or juicy
B	You avoid getting swindled, tricked, or entangled in someone else's trouble
HR
P	<b>RECRUIT</b>
P	When you <b><i>put out word that you're hiring</i></b>, say who you're looking for, what the job is, and what you're offering (the GM will veto if unreasonable). Then roll and add…
E	+1 if your offer is generous;
E	+1 if the work conditions are favorable; and
E	+1 if your reputation around here is solid.
P	<b>On a 10+</b>, you find someone but pick 1; <b>on</b> <b>a 7-9</b>, you find someone but pick 2.
B	They lack some of the skills you wanted
B	They're entangled, impaired, or annoying
B	You draw unwanted attention
B	They have debts or obligations that you need to clear up first
VT	services
VR	A guide around town, for the day	0
VR	Someone to watch things, for a day	0
VR	A laborer's help, for a day	0
VR	A crew of laborers, for a week	1
VR	A bodyguard/muscle, for a few days	1
VR	A consultation with a skilled healer	1
VR	An engineer/foreman, for a big project	2
VR	A skilled healer's care, for a few weeks	2
VR	A fen-walker (page 117) to guide you...	
VR	... to a known, nearby spot	1
VR	... to a dangerous/unknown spot	2
VR	... to a place of almost certain death	3

P	<b>HP</b> 12; <b>Armor</b> 3 (brigandine, shield)

P	• Hide his true strength or position
P	• Out-think and out-maneuver

P	<i>Group</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 2 (iron scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> steel-tipped spear d8 (<i>close</i>, <i>thrown</i>,
P	2 piercing)
P	<b>Ex-Claw instinct</b> to lord over others.
P	• Bully, threaten, intimidate
P	• Cover each other's backs
P	• Demand a bribe or accommodation
P	<b>Loyalist instinct</b> to protect the town, no matter what.
P	• Give fair warning before using force
P	• Stand firm in the face of danger
P	<b>New recruit instinct</b> to avoid danger or punishment.
P	• Shout a warning/order
P	• Hesitate
P	• Look the other way

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Fire
P	Much of Dropoff is susceptible to fire, and Low Town is basically a tinderbox.
P	A building catches fire? Hoo boy.
P	<b>Instinct</b> to consume and spread.
P	• Push them back with a wave of heat (d4 damage)
P	• Fill the area with choking smoke (debilities)
P	• Collapse a burning structure (d8 damage, ignores armor, <i>forceful</i>)
P	• Engulf someone or thing in flames (d10 damage, ignores armor, <i>messy</i>)
P	When <b><i>a building catches fire and it's not</i></b> <b><i>quickly contained</i></b>, start the following:
C	The building is engulfed; cries of alarm
C	A nearby building or two also catch; the original building starts to collapse
C	Many buildings are ablaze; folks panic
C	Fire spreads in multiple directions; palisade catches fire; bedlam
C	<b>Impending doom:</b> Fire burns itself out, scores dead, homes and shops ruined, large parts of the palisade destroyed
ICON	icons/people.svg
H3	Thieves
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> knife d6 (hand, disadvantage)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to get theirs and get gone.
P	• Grab something, slip away unnoticed
P	• Vanish into a crowd or an alley
P	• Spot an easy mark
P	• Wriggle free
P	When you <b><i>go unwary into the bustle</i></b> <b><i>of Edgemarket or the crowded streets of</i></b> <b><i>Dropoff</i></b>, roll +WIS: <b>on a 10+</b>, you spot the pickpocket coming or catch them in the act; <b>on a 7-9</b>, they make off with only trifles (1d4 uses of Supplies, a purse of coppers, a skin of whisky, etc.); <b>on a 6-</b>, whatever they got, you're going to miss it.
